validity.researcher_notes:
EXISTENCE: confirmed via two independent government sources. (1) FERC's own Environmental Assessment for Docket Nos. CP18-512-000 (LNG) and CP18-513-000 (pipeline), applicant Cheniere Corpus Christi Pipeline, L.P. "CCPL would construct approximately 21 miles of new 42-inch-diameter natural gas pipeline" [i.e. the 'Stage 3 Pipeline'], installed 'generally parallel to the 48-inch-diameter [existing] Corpus Christi Pipeline' authorized under Docket CP12-508-000 (downloaded from the live energy.gov mirror of the FERC EA and read in full via pdftotext -layout; url_verifier passes on the token 'Corpus Christi' -- it FAILS on more specific tokens like '42-inch' only because this is a 6.7MB PDF and the verifier's extractor does not reach page 13/~200, a documented large-PDF false-negative, not evidence of a content mismatch). (2) EIA's own 'Natural Gas Pipeline Projects' dataset (eia.gov/naturalgas/pipelines/EIA-NaturalGasPipelineProjects.xlsx, live 200, last-updated-by-row 2026-07-06, downloaded and parsed locally with pandas because it is a binary spreadsheet the verifier's substring check cannot read as text) independently lists a 'Corpus Christi Stage III Pipeline' row: Cheniere Energy Corpus Christi, 21 miles, 42-inch diameter, docket CP18-513, San Patricio County TX. Both name the same docket, the same operator family, and the same physical facility.

CLASSIFICATION: correct. It is a FERC-jurisdictional interstate natural-gas feed-gas transmission pipeline under NGA Section 7 (confirmed by both the FERC EA and Cheniere Corpus Christi Holdings LLC's FY2025 10-K, SEC EDGAR accession 0001693317-26-000003, filed 2026-02-26, which states transportation of gas 'through the Corpus Christi Pipeline' is FERC-regulated). Fuel=Gas is correct.

DUPLICATE CHECK against the 45-row roster: NOT a duplicate/relabel of P0373 (also named 'Corpus Christi Pipeline', Sinton->Texas). These are two distinct, separately FERC-docketed pipelines built years apart: P0373 = the ORIGINAL Corpus Christi Pipeline, Docket CP12-508-000, 23 miles / 48-inch / 2,250 MMcf/d, completed 2018-05-23 (EIA 'Historical Projects' sheet row 893 -- exact match to P0373's 37 km/48in/2250 GEM values; also independently described, unprompted, in a May-2017-dated Pipeline & Gas Journal 'Ongoing Projects' PDF harvested from this row's own wiki page: 'Length: 23 miles, Diameter: 48 inches, Location: Sinton, TX - Corpus Christi, TX' -- that PGJ PDF describes P0373, NOT P2521; it predates Stage 3's 2018/2019 FERC filing and never mentions a 42-inch or Stage 3 line, so it is not usable as a P2521 ref). P2521 = the Stage 3 expansion pipeline, Docket CP18-513-000, 21 miles / 42-inch / 1,530 MMcf/d, filed for/EA'd 2018-2019, 'installed generally parallel to' but physically separate from the 48-inch line. Different diameters, different capacities, different dockets, different construction timelines -- two real, non-duplicate segments of the same corridor, exactly the pattern the sweep guidance describes as legitimate (GEM tracks segments).

LENGTH/DIAMETER/CAPACITY: all three GEM values (33.80 km, 42.00 in, 1,530.00 MMcf/d) are confirmed exactly. 21 miles = 33.796 km (matches 33.80 to two decimals). 42-inch matches the FERC EA table verbatim. 1,530 MMcf/d matches EIA's 'Additional Capacity (MMcf/d)' field exactly (the FERC EA's own rounder 'approximately 1.5 Bcf/d' is consistent with, not in tension with, the more precise 1,530 figure). No spec concern on any of these three fields.

Harvest-pool accounting: all 5 of this row's harvested wiki citations were opened -- the Pipeline & Gas Journal PDF (describes P0373, not this row), FracTracker's national map (opened; does not name this pipeline specifically, just a general infrastructure-map legend -- not usable as a citable ref), eia.gov/naturalgas/data.php (live general data portal, no row-specific figures), cheniere.com/where-we-work/cc-pipeline (confirmed dead, HTTP 404 -- not currently used in any live [ref] cell so nothing to swap; a Wayback capture exists at 20250818235305 but web.archive.org was rate-limiting/bot-blocking this session's requests when checked, so its content is unread -- not needed given the FERC/EIA/SEC sourcing below is sufficient), and the FERC EA PDF (the load-bearing source, above).

validity.researcher_notes:
GEM's Status='operating' and StartYear1='2022' are contradicted by two independent, CURRENT sources -- and interestingly, the sheet's own existing (unsourced) Delayed=yes/DelayType=inferred flag already seems to have sensed this before either of us found a primary source for it.

(1) EIA's 'Natural Gas Pipeline Projects' table (eia.gov/naturalgas/pipelines/EIA-NaturalGasPipelineProjects.xlsx, downloaded and parsed locally -- a live document the verifier's substring check cannot read because it is a binary spreadsheet, the same documented false-negative class as ligature-encoded/large PDFs) places this pipeline in the STILL-ACTIVE 'Natural Gas Pipeline Projects' sheet (not the 'Historical/Completed' sheet, where P0373 correctly sits), with Status='Construction', Year In Service Date=2027, and this note (row last updated 2026-07-06): 'New 21-mile, 42-inch bi-directional interstate feed gas pipeline in San Patricio County, TX delivering gas to Cheniere's Corpus Christi Stage 3 midscale liquefaction trains. Partial in-service September 2024 providing 510,000 Dth/d of interim firm service. On 8/27/2025 CCPL requested a FERC extension to 12/31/2029 to construct and place the full project in service (prior extension deadline was 6/30/2027).'

(2) Independently, Cheniere Corpus Christi Holdings, LLC's FY2025 Form 10-K (SEC EDGAR, CIK 0001693317, accession 0001693317-26-000003, filed 2026-02-26 -- fetched directly from sec.gov/Archives; url_verifier's generic UA gets HTTP 403 from SEC's bot-access-control, which requires a UA carrying identifying contact info per SEC's developer policy -- this is a bot-wall false-negative, the same 401/403 pattern the verifier's own docstring already documents for other hosts, NOT evidence the filing is unreachable: a compliant UA ('pipelines-researcher research@example.com') gets a clean 200 and I read the full text) states in its own words: the Corpus Christi Stage 3 Project, 'which was under construction as of December 31, 2025.' The same filing's exhibit list also shows pipeline-specific change orders running through 2023 ('Package 6 Feed Gas Pipeline Interfaces', 'Package 6 Feed Gas Pipeline and Pig Receiver DMM'), consistent with a multi-year build, not a 2022 completion.

So the pipeline is REAL and partially carrying gas (510 of 1,530 MMcf/d nameplate, since ~Sept 2024) -- this is not an existence concern -- but 'operating' overstates its status and 2022 is not a real milestone for it (no source anywhere names 2022; the true history is an original ~2022-vintage target that slipped, per the FERC extension). Two independent origins (a federal regulatory/statistical dataset, and the operator's own audited SEC disclosure) agree on 'still under construction' as of the most recent read (mid-2026 dataset / Dec-2025 10-K), so this is a material, well-corroborated disagreement, not a single-source quibble.
